answer: Kernel-shaped inlet plume gating: each agent’s request stream enters a per-source inlet, where a sliding-window kernel density estimator scores inter-arrival times and burst dispersion. Admission requires a stable, independent timing plume across epochs; synchronized or batch-generated Sybils fail the shape check and are throttled. Attacker cost: must generate distinct jittered schedules per identity, hold each inlet open over multiple epochs, and absorb idle bandwidth/compute plus rejected admission slots—scaling linearly with each viable Sybil.
